screening_decisions.reason: This is an observational PET imaging study examining receptor binding, not a randomised controlled trial comparing treatment outcomes. No randomisation or treatment comparison.
Randomised double-blind multi-center study comparing amisulpride to flupentixol (typical antipsychotic) in 132 patients with acute schizophrenia. Meets all criteria.
Double-blind randomised study comparing amisulpride to fluphenazine (typical antipsychotic) in 40 hospitalized patients with unproductive/negative schizophrenia. Meets all criteria.
This is a methodological paper describing development of a rating scale, not a clinical trial. No intervention comparison.
This is a Cochrane review about clozapine, not a primary RCT involving amisulpride. Does not meet inclusion criteria.
This is a review article summarizing multiple studies, not a primary randomised controlled trial.
Double-blind randomised study comparing multiple doses of amisulpride to haloperidol (typical antipsychotic) in 319 patients with acute schizophrenia. Meets all criteria.
Methodological paper about developing a depression rating scale, not a clinical trial. No drug intervention comparison.
PET imaging study examining receptor occupancy, not a randomised controlled trial comparing treatment outcomes.
Study primarily evaluates two new experimental drugs (SDZ HDC-912 and OPC-4392), with amisulpride only as a comparator reference. Not primarily comparing amisulpride to standard treatments.
Retrospective economic assessment using chart review, not a prospective randomised controlled trial. Patients were randomly selected for analysis, not randomised to treatment.
Multi-centre randomised parallel-group double-blind study comparing amisulpride to placebo in 141 patients with predominantly negative symptoms of schizophrenia. Meets all criteria.
Multicenter double-blind randomised trial comparing amisulpride to haloperidol (typical antipsychotic) in 191 patients with acute exacerbations of schizophrenia. Meets all criteria.
Placebo-controlled multicenter double-blind randomised trial comparing two doses of amisulpride to placebo in patients with primary negative symptoms of schizophrenia. Meets all criteria.
Study population consists of non-psychotic subjects who never presented psychotic symptoms. Does not meet population criteria (schizophrenia or other non-affective serious mental illnesses).
Methodological paper describing development of an observation scale, not a clinical trial with intervention comparison.
Narrative review article discussing various treatment strategies, not a primary randomised controlled trial.
Randomised study comparing amisulpride to haloperidol (typical antipsychotic) in 60 long-term in-patients with chronic schizophrenia and predominant negative symptoms. Meets all criteria.
Methodological paper describing development and validation of PANSS rating scale, not a clinical trial.
Double-blind randomised study comparing amisulpride to haloperidol (typical antipsychotic) in 41 schizophrenic patients over 42 days. Meets all criteria.
Review article discussing mechanism of action and summarizing evidence, not a primary randomised controlled trial.
Methodological paper describing development of akathisia rating scale, not a clinical trial.

Multicentre double-blind randomised flexible-dose study comparing amisulpride to haloperidol (typical antipsychotic) in 199 patients with paranoid schizophrenia or schizophreniform disorders. Meets all criteria.
Methodological paper describing development of assessment scales, not a clinical trial.
Parallel-group double-blind placebo-controlled randomised trial comparing two doses of amisulpride to placebo in 104 in-patients with schizophrenia and negative symptoms. Meets all criteria.
Review article summarizing published clinical experience with atypical neuroleptics in children/adolescents, not a primary RCT.

While this is an RCT, it compares amisulpride to bromocriptine (dopamine agonist, not an antipsychotic) in infantile autism. Bromocriptine is not a placebo or antipsychotic drug as required by criteria.
Open-label trial (not double-blind) comparing adjunctive treatments in patients already on stable haloperidol. Does not meet RCT design criteria (open trial).
Completely unrelated study about respiratory measurement techniques (airway resistance). Not about schizophrenia or antipsychotic drugs.
Methodological paper describing modification of EPS rating scale, not a clinical trial.
Open clinical study (not randomised or controlled). Abstract only mentions pharmacological screening findings, no RCT design described.
